methodology.commit_counts: Unique commits reachable from the pinned default-branch head, including merges. Attribution partitions this total. user_work separately deduplicates attributable SHAs across its stated scope; these two counts must not be subtracted from one another.
methodology.last_commit: Default-branch tip and its Git committer timestamp; not GitHub pushed_at. User activity and sustained-work dates use authored timestamps converted to UTC.
methodology.last_sustained_work: Latest inclusive 14-calendar-day window with at least five attributable nonmerge commits on at least three distinct UTC dates. Null means no qualifying window was observed, not proof of no sustained effort.
methodology.confirmed_identity: GitHub maps the author/coauthor to the authenticated account, or the address exactly matches one linked to that account elsewhere in the evidence. Actual addresses are not exported.
methodology.inferred_identity: RA/ra local or email-less signatures, or a numpde-address signature, observed in account-owned repositories. External attribution requires an exact nonempty address/signature match or the same SHA in owned history. These are plausible identity matches, not cryptographic proof.
methodology.other_authors: A different linked GitHub account or a distinct noncandidate author signature; automation is classified separately where recognized. Unclassified large-history commits are not presumed to be other humans.
methodology.coauthorship: GitHub author lists (up to ten names per commit) and local Co-authored-by trailers identify shared contributions. A commit may count once in user_work and also be marked shared; effort shares are not inferred from author order.
methodology.forks: The default branch is compared against a pinned current parent default branch. User SHAs also reachable from that parent are marked inherited; distinct-from-parent does not prove sole original authorship. Upstream-merged work can move into the inherited category.
methodology.difficulty: Contribution difficulty is distinct from whole-repository complexity. Generic small-patch estimates based on codebase scope or commit counts were withdrawn. Unknown is null. Merged project scores are not sums or maxima of repository estimates.
methodology.amount_of_work: 0-100 historical effort estimate. Initial activity proxy: min(100, round(15*log10(1+nonmerge_commits) + 18*log10(1+active_days) + 5*log10(1+active_months))), excluding current-parent inherited SHAs. Curated overrides explain bulk imports and work not represented by commit frequency. This is not hours, remaining work, or productivity.
methodology.assessment_refresh: Existing descriptions, categories, keywords, and all assessment objects are preserved. Their assessed_at timestamps can precede measured-field refreshes; reassess them deliberately after reviewing new evidence.
methodology.privacy: Only repository identity/visibility, GitHub links, aggregate activity, user alias names, and sanitized descriptions are exported. Raw addresses, commit messages, file contents, credentials, host addresses, and runtime configuration remain outside the checkout. Attributable commit SHAs are exported for exact deduplication; raw signatures and messages remain private.
methodology.projects: Project records own graph identity and semantic descriptions. Every repository belongs to exactly one project. Membership is an editorial decision, not automatic fork collapse. Repository history, visibility, attribution, and subjective estimates remain on repository records.
methodology.project_contributions: Project user_work is derived from the union of member repositories user_work.commit_shas, with earliest/latest observed activity. Global unique work is the union across all repository SHA sets, not the sum of repository or project counts. Equal SHAs are deduplicated; rebased or cherry-picked changes with different SHAs are not presumed identical.
methodology.project_embeddings: Project description, domain keywords, and optional substantive methods only. Names, owners, reference/fork boilerplate, contribution-count statements, activity metrics, generic work contexts, broad theme labels, and curated edges are excluded.

identities.evidence: GitHub commit author/coauthor mappings plus cross-repository local signature continuity; private raw evidence is retained outside this checkout.
identities.limitations: Git attribution does not distinguish hand-written, agent-assisted, generated, or automatically committed work under the same identity.

collection.method: Read-only GitHub API queries and existing local Git objects; documentation and selected files support the retained annotations.

links.explanation: The bounded Hardhat prototype could isolate contract interaction/deployment questions before adding payout-policy state. No shared contract behavior or direct project succession is claimed.

links.explanation: A preprint digest pushes newly found literature toward a reader; ISBN lookup starts with a known item and recovers structured metadata. These are different entry points into a literature workflow.

links.explanation: A searchable bibliography could anchor chemical claims to literature while molecule/shift viewers make the subject inspectable. Record-to-structure linking would need to be added; no integration is asserted.

links.explanation: Graph-analysis routines and GNN experiments make topology central but place computation in explicit algorithms or learned representations. This is independent of the fork's small personal patch.

additional_interpretations.explanation: Graph analysis manipulates known topology, while GNN experiments learn representations over it; both make relational structure a primary modeling choice.

links.label: A portfolio's claims can lead to inspectable scientific artifacts
links.explanation: Repository-level summaries describe the work; shared slides, thesis material, and predictions provide artifacts a reader can inspect. This does not treat a presentation as independent scientific validation.

links.explanation: Grammar parsing and lint/format implementation meet at turning source text into structure that rules can inspect. Ruff is not claimed to use Lark.

links.explanation: Invocation-aware metaprogramming changes behavior based on source form, while strict lint policy favors mechanically inspectable conventions. This identifies a design tension, not a verified lint failure.

links.explanation: Neural translation and speech synthesis both map structured input sequences to outputs with alignment and representation choices; speech introduces an acoustic modality rather than another written language.

links.label: Time-dependent diffusion problems become tractable through solver structure
links.explanation: Preconditioned mean-field-game optimization and space-time wavelet/multigrid methods both exploit operator structure to control difficult time-dependent computations. They solve different mathematical problems.

links.label: Stability matters when numerical dynamics represent a moment equation
links.explanation: Stochastic-ODE second-moment computation and Runge-Kutta stability study both concern whether a discretization preserves meaningful evolving behavior. Their specific stability criteria are not assumed identical.

links.explanation: Bayesian-network uncertainty could motivate a surrogate alternative in acquisition-driven optimization. This is a methodological experiment, not an assertion that the image-classification model is directly usable as a surrogate.

links.label: Choose an informative evaluation or learn an action policy
links.explanation: Bayesian optimization selects evaluations under uncertainty; lunar-lander learning selects actions whose consequences change future state. Both are sequential decisions with different feedback and objectives.

links.label: From configuration sketches to calibrated geometry
links.explanation: The browser design prototype and calibrated CAD workflow increase emphasis on units, geometric meaning, exports, and dimensional checks. This does not assert that every earlier interface feature is preserved.

links.label: Connect requested specifications to a manufacturable geometry
links.explanation: A demand/configuration prototype and parametric CAD could relate user requests to explicit geometric parameters and exportable designs. Manufacturing suitability and accepted parameter ranges would require separate work.

links.label: Make financial reasoning visible as a decision structure
links.explanation: The graphical NPV tool makes assumptions and alternative outcomes inspectable, complementing mathematical finance notes. It does not implement or illustrate every model in those notes.

links.label: Express what another party is permitted to do
links.explanation: Photograph-use preferences and executable token authorization both articulate permission. A displayed license and an enforced authorization decision have different legal and technical effects.

links.label: Relate digital statements to real-world rights
links.explanation: Photo-use terms and bicycle ownership records raise a common question: what a digital declaration establishes about rights over an external object. Neither a QR code nor a chain entry alone settles every real-world claim.

links.label: Make personal usage preferences expressible
links.explanation: Cookie-consent automation and photo-use licenses both try to make individual preferences legible to systems or other people. Preference expression and actual compliance remain distinct.

links.label: Bound effects at the point where they are requested
links.explanation: Popup interception and agent sandboxing put control around operations before allowing their effects. Their threat models and enforceable boundaries are very different.

links.label: Pre-limit authority or approve an operation explicitly
links.explanation: A disposable container with constrained access and a host-command approval terminal illustrate distinct control points: predefined execution authority and review of a proposed effect. These mechanisms can also be combined.

links.label: Keep a proposal separate from authority to apply it
links.explanation: A cleanup preview/preparation lane and an agent host-command queue both make proposed work inspectable before granting the authority to execute a change.

links.label: Detect misleading behavior and limit possible damage
links.explanation: Deception-detection experiments ask about a model's behavior; sandboxing limits available effects regardless of whether a model appears trustworthy. They address different parts of the trust problem.

links.label: Challenge the assumption that a plausible explanation is correct
links.explanation: Deception-oriented experiments could motivate evaluation of confident but misleading error explanations. A detector trained in one setting cannot be assumed to recognize false explanations in another.

links.label: Explain a failure in prose or constrain an actionable interpretation
links.explanation: Error explanation seeks a useful natural-language account; application-aware tool-call data seeks interpretations that satisfy explicit schemas and domain boundaries. Fluency and executable correctness are distinct objectives.

links.label: Make permitted operations explicit in a tiny interface
links.explanation: A read-only mapping wrapper isolates a small distinction between reading and mutating state. Authorization systems address richer versions of the question of which operations are available to whom. The wrapper is not a security boundary by itself.

links.label: Make the boundary part of the interface
links.explanation: An inclusive range API exposes endpoint semantics; authorization code exposes authority and validity boundaries. The common principle is making consequential boundary choices explicit rather than relying on a reader's assumption.

links.label: Share contributions without erasing their boundaries
links.explanation: Encrypted mailbox retrieval and provenance-aware research-data sharing both raise questions about how independently supplied information is retained and disclosed. Their privacy guarantees and data models are not interchangeable.

links.label: Specify an interaction so independent clients can interpret it
links.explanation: Signed purchase formats and application manifests make parts of an interaction explicit outside one particular client. Both require a distinction between describing an operation and having authority to perform it.

links.label: Encryption primitives and a mailbox confidentiality boundary
links.explanation: Hybrid-encryption tooling concerns cryptographic message representation; an encrypted-mail service must also decide what is stored, who may retrieve it, and which metadata remains exposed. Primitive selection alone does not answer the service-level question.

links.label: Make the signed meaning explicit
links.explanation: Typed Ethereum signing structures and signed payment wire profiles both bind a particular representation to a signature. Their serialization, domain separation, and trust rules must be evaluated in their own protocols.

links.label: Aggregate explicit votes or model interacting choices
links.explanation: A voting service records expressed decisions; a mean-field-game model reasons about choices shaped by interactions. Both concern collective outcomes, through very different mechanisms and assumptions.

links.label: Give a signed decision a human-facing interaction
links.explanation: The voting interface turns a signed polling workflow into a concrete browser interaction, making a protocol-level capability accessible to a participant.

links.label: Exchange explicit units across independent participants
links.explanation: Federated model-state exchange and agent mail require a sender and receiver to agree on the meaning and identity of an exchanged unit without assuming shared process memory. Their consistency and confidentiality requirements differ.

links.label: Keep derived information accountable to its source
links.explanation: Analytical transcription preserves source-written evidence; chain indexing must track which chain history supports a derived record. Both make origin and revision consequential, with different meanings of canonicality.

links.label: Curate a reusable reference or preserve a source observation
links.explanation: A compact reference distribution and faithful paper-level extraction support different stages of research data use. Licensing, version identity, and source provenance remain important in both.

links.label: Retain the origin of scientific contributions
links.explanation: A proposed AMR-sharing platform and a characterization corpus both make the origin of each scientific contribution important to later reuse. A shared principle does not imply a shared schema or implementation.

links.label: Keep the scientific record correctable
links.explanation: Published corrections and source-faithful extraction both preserve a distinction between the record and later judgments about it. Their roles differ: correcting an author's account and representing what a source actually says.

links.label: A standalone indexer and an existing indexing framework
links.explanation: Both address recovering and interpreting chain history, but organizing a standalone system and modifying a framework permit different design choices. This link makes no claim of code descent or a measured superiority.

links.label: Retain progress and evidence across interruptions
links.explanation: A chain indexer and a provider-delivery runtime both need to preserve meaningful progress when processes or peers become unavailable. Canonical-chain recovery and result delivery have different effect and retry semantics.

links.label: Separate communication delay from application timing
links.explanation: Timestamping send and receive phases could help distinguish where observed order-book latency originates. Instrumentation must not be mistaken for proof of remote market timing.

links.label: Make an invisible temporal effect measurable
links.explanation: Battery event logging and staged pipe timestamps turn behavior that is hard to observe directly into time-indexed evidence. Their sampling and instrumentation limitations differ.

links.label: Move a model into an independently operated service
links.explanation: Scientific model development and provider-runtime work confront different obligations: prediction semantics versus job lifecycles, interpretation, delivery, and operational control.

links.label: Turn a research capability into a usable service workflow
links.explanation: A thesis-centered inference workflow and a signed job platform illustrate the additional structure needed to expose scientific computation to independent users and providers. This does not assert that the API deploys the thesis model itself.

links.label: Make a published prediction method reproducible and inspectable
links.explanation: The provider/reproduction project surrounds an existing scientific model with explicit inputs, scientific guidance, execution conditions, and service integration. Original model research remains upstream work.

links.label: Turn a research system into a bounded analysis offering
links.explanation: The deployment project narrows scientific input routes and operational behavior around an upstream model, making its capabilities available through a provider interface.

links.label: Make a structure-search method an operable provider
links.explanation: Repackaging and provider integration address how a scientific search method can be run, controlled, and delivered as a service. This is an operational progression, not a claim of scientific improvement over upstream.

links.label: Make scientific jobs and their outcomes inspectable
links.explanation: A browser workspace gives users a way to organize and inspect analysis performed by model providers. It exposes a scientific workflow rather than making the learned model internally interpretable by itself.

links.label: Put a scientific service workflow into a concrete demonstration
links.explanation: The build-week application combines model proposals, a workspace, and the signed API into a concrete molecular-debugging demonstration, making the scientific service workflow inspectable as an application.

links.label: Ask whether component contracts compose into a scientific workflow
links.explanation: The design repository proposes cross-service acceptance scenarios around APIs, transfers, edges, and providers. This is a planned test relationship; no implemented runner is asserted.

links.label: Isolate federated training before formalizing state exchange
links.explanation: A two-client Flower experiment offers a limited setting for concepts that become explicit in a deterministic federated-learning backbone. The link does not assert shared code or a particular migration path.

links.label: Probe API-to-tool interactions in a small service setting
links.explanation: Shared HTTP execution and OpenAPI/MCP bridge experiments can isolate interaction questions relevant to an agent-facing mail service. This is a conceptual test setting, not a claim that the mail service is built from those examples.

links.label: Experiment with reactive interaction in a smaller interface
links.explanation: ReactPy exercises offer a bounded environment for learning about stateful interface behavior relevant to more substantial browser workspaces. The actual frontend technologies and architectures differ.

links.label: Service-specific authority and reusable token semantics
links.explanation: The signed scientific API and token authorization core expose the tension between concrete service rules and a reusable permission model. Their overlap does not establish substitutability or current adoption.

links.label: Turn engineering principles into reusable working instructions
links.explanation: A collection of software-development goals and agent skills differ in how directly they guide a particular task. The progression concerns applicability of instructions, not a claim that every skill derives from those goals.

links.label: Guide behavior and bound the available authority
links.explanation: Instructions influence how a coding agent should work; a constrained execution environment controls which effects it can cause. Instruction compliance and mechanical isolation are different kinds of assurance.

links.label: Define strict code rules or control how cleanup is applied
links.explanation: A linting ruleset and a cleanup-authority experiment answer different parts of code maintenance: which changes are desirable, and how a proposed change may reach the repository.

links.label: Place automated cleanup inside an explicit effect boundary
links.explanation: A fast linting/formatting engine supplies a capability; the cleanup experiment asks how to constrain previews, preparation, and application. This is a step in operational control rather than a claim of improving the linter.

links.label: Make host identity and access boundaries explicit
links.explanation: UID/GID mapping tools and constrained agent launchers both require concrete understanding of what container execution can access on the host. Identity mapping and broader sandbox policy remain different responsibilities.

links.label: Package a recurrent installation concern as a small helper
links.explanation: Both repositories include a resilient Conda-installation helper. They show a recurring environment-management concern expressed as a focused utility; no direction of code transfer is asserted.

links.label: Keep maintenance effects within an explicit scope
links.explanation: Host/container retention and repository cleanup both make the scope of a maintenance action important. A useful default is to identify the resource and authority before applying a destructive or mutating operation.

links.label: Move inference capability into an accessible local service
links.explanation: Inference implementation and local serving/chat deployment concern different stages of making language models useful. This does not assert that the current service uses the fork's custom branch.

links.label: Run a model and coordinate a shared inference environment
links.explanation: Model-serving experiments expose backend behavior; systemd-based runners, ingress, and GPU sharing address how multiple capabilities coexist. The relation concerns operational questions, not identical deployment configuration.

links.label: Bring an opaque remote computation into a browser workspace
links.explanation: A local-model assistant and an NMR analysis workspace both translate a computational service into an interaction a person can inspect. Their domain semantics and authorization models differ.

links.label: Probe which application state may be ephemeral
links.explanation: A split-database probe could inform questions about separating framework state from durable domain records in a service. It does not demonstrate mail durability, nor does volatile storage become suitable for mailbox data through this analogy.

links.label: Connect local papers to a searchable research workspace
links.explanation: Consistent PDF naming and a bibliography interface could reduce the effort of moving between a citation and the local paper being read. Reliable identifiers and reconciliation would be needed.

links.label: Discover new papers and organize an existing literature set
links.explanation: A preprint digest addresses incoming literature; a bibliography workspace supports revisiting and organizing known references. They serve different temporal parts of research reading.

links.label: Enrich a literature workspace with library metadata
links.explanation: ISBN-based bibliographic lookup could supply metadata for books in a research bibliography, complementing paper-oriented records. Matching and provenance would need to remain explicit.

links.label: Retrieve content on demand or curate a scientific record
links.explanation: On-demand web retrieval and paper-level source-faithful extraction answer different needs: immediate access to content and deliberate creation of reusable evidence. Retrieval alone does not establish faithful scientific extraction.

links.label: Access measurements and organize their biological interpretation
links.explanation: Genomic-data utilities and gene-set references support distinct parts of an analysis: obtaining observations and relating genes to interpretable groupings. No particular enrichment workflow is asserted.

links.label: From exercises to an open method-comparison project
links.explanation: Course exercises and a collaborative tissue-deconvolution study move from bounded assignments to choices about methods, comparisons, and interpretation.

links.label: Carry sequence-modeling questions into a physical science
links.explanation: Legal-text coursework and molecular language-model research both ask how meaning can be represented in sequences. Chemistry adds structural equivalence and experimental constraints that text modeling does not supply automatically.

links.label: Preserve meaning while changing its written representation
links.explanation: A mathematical translation and Braille conversions change how meaning is written or accessed. Natural-language mathematical interpretation and character-level conversion carry very different ambiguity and fidelity obligations.

links.label: Encode human meaning through different physical modalities
links.explanation: Braille notation and acoustic finger-input recognition explore different interfaces between symbols and physical interaction. This is a modality connection, not a claim that the acoustic prototype is an accessibility device.

links.label: Give generated stories a controllable spoken form
links.explanation: A story/video prototype and a speech-synthesis toolkit could form a richer audiovisual generation workflow. Voice licensing, model compatibility, and timing would need separate treatment.

links.label: Identify content or authenticate a statement
links.explanation: A content identifier identifies particular bytes; a signed purchase statement also depends on signer identity and trust. The comparison makes explicit that content integrity and authorization answer different questions.

links.label: Use call-site structure to extend how Python expresses intent
links.explanation: Source-aware callables and a pipeline-operator experiment both exploit the relationship between source syntax and runtime behavior. They provide different language affordances and have different limitations.

links.label: Study isolated contract behavior before composing an application
links.explanation: Small Solidity examples isolate contract mechanisms that become part of a larger manifest-driven application and workflow. This is a learning relationship, not an assertion about copied implementations.

links.label: Isolate wallet interaction from application semantics
links.explanation: A wallet test application can expose transaction and provider behavior in a smaller setting than a generic contract-defined application viewer. No shared test harness is asserted.

links.label: Generalize one ownership application into describable workflows
links.explanation: Bicycle registration supplies a concrete ownership problem; the manifest-based protocol considers how multiple contract-defined applications can describe their interactions to generic viewers. The comparison concerns scope rather than verified code lineage.

links.label: Attach digital records to art or to physical property
links.explanation: An art-oriented smart-contract prototype and bicycle registration expose different questions about what a token refers to and how its digital state relates to an external asset. The exact rights conveyed depend on the application.

links.label: Describe an exchange and decide when it is settled
links.explanation: Marketplace interaction experiments and service-purchase accounting address different forms of exchange. Both need a distinction between an offered action, an accepted commitment, and the resulting state change.

links.label: A promise on a contract and an accounted service purchase
links.explanation: A pledge-contract prototype and service accounting expose different ways of representing commitments and fulfillment. Their mechanisms are not assumed to have identical settlement semantics.

links.label: Separate attribution from permission to use an image
links.explanation: A credited image slideshow and photo-use preferences highlight different parts of image reuse. Showing a source credit and conveying the relevant permissions are separate questions; no legal assessment of either project is implied.

links.label: Expose relationships so a collection becomes navigable
links.explanation: A repository inventory and a graph of software-development practices can turn separate entries into a map of meaningful relationships. The value comes from explained links rather than a list of labels.

links.label: Different measurement technologies, related expression questions
links.explanation: Raw microarray preprocessing and genomic-data utilities support different routes to gene-expression evidence. They can illuminate how measurement technology and preprocessing shape a downstream biological interpretation.

links.label: A reference population gives an enrichment result its context
links.explanation: An enrichment method and its reference data expose two parts of a statistical claim: the procedure and the population against which a gene list is interpreted. The reference choice affects what the result can mean.

links.label: A method-centered interface and a multi-provider workspace
links.explanation: A SECS-focused elucidation interface and a workspace for jobs across providers organize scientific interaction at different scopes. The comparison concerns how users encounter a method and its results, not which frontend is better.

links.label: Control which interruptions enter the user workflow
links.explanation: Suppressing a desktop switching overlay and intercepting browser popups both change when interruptions are presented. Desktop distraction and adversarial browser behavior have different causes and control requirements.

embedding_review.scope: Every one of the 213 repositories was reviewed against its embedding-generated neighbors, including nodes for which no additional link was justified. The 561-edge embedded graph supplied candidates; it did not select curated relationships or generate their explanations.
embedding_review.candidate_rule: Union of the 2% all-pairs cosine-distance cutoff and each repository's two nearest neighbors, deduplicated as undirected pairs.
embedding_review.selection: Added a link when the endpoint evidence supported a specific shared problem, contrasting inference target, complementary responsibility, interpretive bridge, or plausible concrete transfer. Existing links were preserved. Proposed integrations and experiments remain prospective; upstream content does not become personal authorship.
embedding_review.not_added: Nonselection does not assert that two repositories are unrelated. Fork ancestry is already represented by lineage. Generic technology, shared maintenance vocabulary, undocumented placeholders, and additional same-topic connections without a distinct insight were insufficient reasons to make the curated graph denser.

examples_not_added.reason: Cell-expression annotation and Braille conversion have different subject matter; the embedding match does not provide a useful shared problem or transfer.
Hardware-driver packaging and microarray preprocessing both have maintenance history, but that alone supplies no substantive semantic link.
Two poorly documented stubs do not reveal a shared implemented purpose. Adding an edge solely because both are placeholders would add little meaning.
The same upstream method and shared bug-fix history are already accounted for by lineage and attribution; a duplicate ancestry edge is unnecessary.

embedding_review.stage: Historical review of the repository-node graph, before project consolidation.

node_review.scope: Each repository was considered individually for purpose, attributable work summary, focused work keywords, themes, work contexts, and semantic neighbors before preparing the richer embedding input. Summaries use inspected descriptions and contribution evidence; lack of identified commits is not proof that no work occurred.
node_review.uncertainty: Empty theme/context memberships remain where purpose is insufficiently documented. Proposed uses of placeholders are low-confidence prospective edges, not recovered project history.
node_review.embedding_projection: Project description, domain keywords, and optional substantive methods only. Names, owners, reference/fork boilerplate, contribution-count statements, activity metrics, generic work contexts, broad theme labels, and curated edges are excluded.

semantic_graph.scope: Curated semantic relationships between projects. Individual repository records retain lineage, measurements, attribution, and provenance. Evidence references still address repository IDs and fields.

basis_definitions.established: An explicit relationship is supported by the inventoried project descriptions or reviewed documentation. This is documentary evidence, not a runtime or scientific qualification result.
basis_definitions.interpretive: An editorial reading of the endpoint topics or methods. It does not assert historical influence, direct code reuse, a shared dataset, adoption, or measured superiority.
basis_definitions.prospective: A proposed combination, experiment, test, or transfer. The benefit is a hypothesis and no working integration is asserted.

semantic_graph.confidence_definition: Confidence in the stated relationship or its plausibility. For prospective links, high confidence is not a probability of successful implementation or scientific benefit.
semantic_graph.strength_definition: Editorial salience from 0 to 1: how central or illuminating this connection is for this inventory. Independent of confidence, measured effort, and evidence basis.
semantic_graph.work_context_definition: Overlapping editorial descriptions of the form or purpose of repository work; academic, exploratory, toy, and applied contexts can coexist. They are not deployment status or quality rankings.
semantic_graph.theme_definition: Recurring questions that cut across domains. theme_ids are editorial memberships, not automatic keyword matches; membership alone does not establish every possible pairwise link. The measurement-dynamics theme includes observing evolving software and host behavior as well as physical models.
semantic_graph.evidence_definition: References use existing repository IDs and field names. Endpoint descriptions establish the compared subjects; explanations carry the additional interpretation or proposal. Follow each endpoint evidence.reviewed_files for the underlying inspected files.

presentation.edges: Use links[].source and target; arrow direction comes from link_types[type].directed. Symmetric edges are stored once, in canonical endpoint order.
presentation.labels: Use projects[].name for node labels; links[].label/explanation and additional_interpretations retain curated insights.
presentation.optional_theme_nodes: Repository theme memberships remain editorial metadata. They do not determine project identity or project embedding text.
presentation.mechanical_lineage: Repository lineage remains on repositories[].lineage; fork relations are not project-semantic edges.
presentation.filtering: Allow filtering by work context, theme, relationship type, evidence basis, confidence, and repository visibility. A low-connectivity repository may simply have insufficient evidence for an interesting link.
presentation.layout: No layout positions or UI implementation are stored. The graph remains usable by Cytoscape, D3, or another HTML renderer through a small data projection.
presentation.project_nodes: Use projects[].id and name for graph nodes; projects[].repository_ids locate the underlying repository records. Repository IDs are evidence and history identities, not graph nodes.

project_identity_review.policy: Preserve separately purposed adaptations and substantial independent forks; collapse same-project copies. Original relationship IDs and additional explanations remain on coalesced links.
